title: A subclass record inherits parent properties unless an override is written
summary: A narrow taxonomy model treats a shared head as a parent class: a child entry inherits one predeclared property, and an explicit modifier is required to override it.

design.unit: paired parent/child entries sharing a head and a separately observed property
design.contrast: inherited property versus independently repeated property
design.prediction: Across held parent/child pairs, the child should show the parent property without repeating its marker; a written override should be the only allowed way to reverse it.
design.countermodel: The same surface pattern could arise from a context-conditioned lexical convention or editorial packaging without the proposed semantic mechanism.
design.falsifier: A child reverses the parent property with no override, or an override leaves the property unchanged in matched pairs.
design.principal_risk: Parenthood and properties need independently bound source observations; no gold binding is assumed. Near hierarchy/whole-form cards, but the falsifier concerns inheritance and override, not shared topology.
